subject: Request: Leadership consent for Orion Health hosted API rate exception
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: leadership consent for Orion Health hosted API rate exception

Stephanie —

Quick ask: Orion (Emily Wu in procurement) is pushing for a 25% off list rate for Hosted API usage as part of a 12‑month onboarding pilot that immediately expands into a multi‑year commercial agreement. Highlights: 
- Committed ramp to ~5B tokens/month by month 9 if pilot hits engagement metrics (POC targets attached).
- Asking for 25% off on token rates + 90 day net payment terms.
- They also want marketplace listing and a co‑marketing intro to their provider network.

Attached: pricing model (shows unit economics at 25% + cache & batching assumptions) and the signed MOU (pilot terms, not the final SOW). If we deny the deeper concession they will walk to Competitor X (they signaled price sensitivity).

Why I think exec involvement is warranted: this exceeds our standard delegated discount band (>20% needs leadership sign‑off), and the deal size if realized is strategic (healthcare network distribution). My recommendation: approve 25% off for a 12‑month pilot conditioned on: standard DPA/Security questionnaire completion, 1.5M USD minimum committed spend or mutual milestone triggers, and procurement on standard SOW + no additional data residency concessions.

Can you weigh in / escalate to Kar thik and Marcus for signoff? Need an answer by EOD tomorrow to keep momentum.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: orion_pricing_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), orion_mou_signed.pdf (pdf stub)

Team — forwarding Ben's note and attachments. TL;DR: Orion requests a 25% off hosted token rate + 90 day terms for a 12‑month pilot that could convert to a multi‑year, high‑volume commitment.

Why this is time sensitive: procurement has tentatively prioritized Redwood in their vendor short‑list; if we stall they will escalate to Competitor X for a comparable concession. Ben has asked for leadership signoff because this request is outside his delegated band (>20%).

My assessment / ask: 
- I support the 25% concession conditioned on finance/legal gating items (minimum committed spend or milestone triggers, standard legal terms, and completed security questionnaire).
- Please confirm whether to approve now (so I can give procurement a yes with conditions) or if you want to counteroffer (e.g., 20% + co‑marketing budget).

If I don't hear back by tomorrow EOD I will escalate to CFO and Sales Ops.

— Stephanie
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: leadership consent for Orion Health hosted API rate exception

Team —

Thanks for the concise framing. I reviewed the attached pricing model and ran a quick sensitivity against our typical unit economics (with conservative cache assumptions). Notes and decision path: 
- I am comfortable approving up to 25% off list for Hosted API usage in this case, provided the following are locked before signatures: 
  1) Minimum committed spend of 1.5M USD over 12 months OR clear, measurable milestones that escalate committed spend to that level by month 6;
  2) Payment terms capped at Net 60 (we should avoid 90 days unless finance agrees to a one‑time accommodation);
  3) No exceptional data residency or custody concessions beyond our standard DPA; any additional legal asks must be routed to Legal and will be evaluated separately;
  4) Marketplace listing and co‑marketing commitments should be limited to an approved one‑page case study + joint webinar within 6 months.

Please confirm Ben will update HubSpot and that Sales Ops will circulate a short summary for Finance and Legal to sign off operational gating items. If all gates are satisfied I approve the 25% concession for this deal.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Americas (acting)
Redwood Inference

Karthik / Stephanie —

Thanks for the analysis. I'm signing off on the 25% concession under the conditions Karthik outlined with one addition: require a clause that commits Orion to a quarterly business review with Sales + Customer Success for the first 12 months and a termination clause if usage ramps do not meet the agreed milestones (protects us on over‑discounted spend). 

Monica, please work with Legal to fold those gating items into the SOW/SLA and confirm whether Finance can accept Net 60 vs Net 90. Ben — once Legal confirms the language, get DocuSign ready and update the HubSpot deal with the final concession details and the deal value assumption (we're assuming $1.5M committed for approval).
